notice: Four proposed corrections or clarified variants for original Unit 6 Topic 6.4 questions. These are reviewable suggestions, not approved edits. The source bank and all existing answer letters remain unchanged; teacher decision required before any production bank variant, textbook-exact claim, or official FBISE exam certification.

cases.originalFieldText: Its speed increases while approximately the same water volume passes each level per
cases.proposedText: Its speed increases while approximately the same water volume passes each level per second
cases.reason: Public answer option B ends with an unfinished 'per'. The teacher-prepared master text ends 'per second'. This is a direct missing-word import error, not an answer-key dispute.
cases.sourceEvidence: Prepared teacher master PDF p.140, as reconciled in V95-C2N; printed NBF pp.96–99 were not needed to prove this prepared-master copying omission.
cases.physicsCheck: For an approximately steady incompressible falling stream, area A decreases as speed v increases when Av is approximately constant; free-fall acceleration provides the speed increase.

cases.originalFieldText: A main stream (area 2 cm2; speed 5 m s-1) divides into two equal branches of area 1 cm2 each. Branch speed is:
cases.proposedText: A main stream (area 2 cm2; speed 5 m s-1) divides into two equal branches of area 1 cm2 each, with equal volume flow rate through both branches. Speed in either branch is:
cases.reason: Equal outlet areas alone do not mathematically require equal discharge. State equal volume flow to justify the unique selected branch speed.
cases.sourceEvidence: Teacher-prepared master PDF p.143 and V95-C2O. No claim of exact original NBF example phrasing.
cases.physicsCheck: 2×5=1×(v1+v2), so v1+v2=10. Equal split gives v1=v2=5 m/s; unequal v1=3 and v2=7 m/s also conserves total flow.

cases.originalFieldText: NBF Example 6.3: Aorta radius 0.8 cm, speed 0.33 m s-1; blood enters 30 arteries each radius 0.4 cm. Speed in each artery is:
cases.proposedText: Based on the idealized equal-flow split in NBF Example 6.3: Aorta radius 0.8 cm, speed 0.33 m s-1; blood enters 30 arteries, each of radius 0.4 cm, with equal volume flow through each artery. Speed in each artery is:
cases.reason: Printed Example 6.3 numerical data and computed 0.044 m/s are source-verified, but the individually determined outlet speed requires an equal-discharge model; do not imply equal radii alone establish this.
cases.sourceEvidence: Original NBF printed pp.98–99 Example 6.3 numerical givens and answer v2=0.044 m/s directly checked in V95-C2S addendum. Teacher master p.143. The printed book's idealized single v2 is not physical proof that equal radii entail equal flow.
cases.physicsCheck: For equal flow, 0.33×(0.8/0.4)^2/30=0.044 m/s. With unequal branch flow only the sum of 30 outlet flows is fixed.

cases.originalFieldText: One vessel (radius 1 cm) divides into 50 equal vessels (radius 0.1 cm). If initial speed is 0.20 m s-1 and flow is conserved, branch speed is:
cases.proposedText: One vessel (radius 1 cm) divides into 50 equal-radius vessels (radius 0.1 cm), with equal volume flow rate through each branch. If initial speed is 0.20 m s-1 and the fluid is approximately incompressible, speed in each branch is:
cases.reason: Equal branch radii plus mass conservation fix total discharge, not the speed of each branch. State equal division and incompressible conditions explicitly.
cases.sourceEvidence: Teacher-prepared master PDF p.145 and V95-C2P; no claim that Q67 is a verbatim NBF question.
cases.physicsCheck: If flows are equal, v=0.20×(1/0.1)^2/50=0.40 m/s. A distribution with 25 outlets at 0.20 m/s and 25 at 0.60 m/s also conserves the same total volume flow.
